```lean
  [Category.{u₁, u₂} C] [IsPreconnected J] {X Y : C} (α : (Functor.const J).obj X ⟶ (Functor.const J).obj Y)
  (j j' : J) : α.app j = α.app j'
```
***
For objects `X Y : C`, any natural transformation `α : const X ⟶ const Y` from a connected
category must be constant.
This is the key property of connected categories which we use to establish properties about limits.

```lean
Eq.symm.{u} {α : Sort u} {a b : α} (h : a = b) : b = a
```
***
Equality is symmetric: if `a = b` then `b = a`.

Because this is in the `Eq` namespace, if you have a variable `h : a = b`,
`h.symm` can be used as shorthand for `Eq.symm h` as a proof of `b = a`.

For more information: [Equality](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/quantifiers_and_equality.html#equality)

```lean
CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.hom_ext.{v₁, v₃, u₁, u₃} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {C : Type u₃}
  [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] {F : J ⥤ C} {t : Cone F} (h : IsLimit t) {W : C} {f f' : W ⟶ t.pt}
  (w : ∀ (j : J), f ≫ t.π.app j = f' ≫ t.π.app j) : f = f'
```
***
Two morphisms into a limit are equal if their compositions with
each cone morphism are equal.

*import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Comma.Over*

```lean
CategoryTheory.createsLimitOfReflectsIso.{w', w, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {J : Type w} [Category.{w', w} J] {K : J ⥤ C} {F : C ⥤ D} [F.ReflectsIsomorphisms]
  (h : (c : Cone (K ⋙ F)) → (t : IsLimit c) → LiftsToLimit K F c t) : CreatesLimit K F
```
***
If `F` reflects isomorphisms and we can lift any limit cone to a limit cone,
then `F` creates limits.
In particular here we don't need to assume that F reflects limits.

*import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Creates*

```lean
CategoryTheory.Over.CreatesConnected.raiseCone.{v, u} {J : Type v} [SmallCategory J] {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [IsConnected J] {B : C} {F : J ⥤ Over B} (c : Cone (F ⋙ forget B)) : Cone F
```
***
(Impl) Given a cone in the base category, raise it to a cone in the over category. Note this is
where the connected assumption is used.

```lean
CategoryTheory.eqToIso.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (p : X = Y) : X ≅ Y
```
***
An equality `X = Y` gives us an isomorphism `X ≅ Y`.

It is typically better to use this, rather than rewriting by the equality then using `Iso.refl _`
which usually leads to dependent type theory hell.

```lean
CategoryTheory.hasLimit_of_created.{w', w, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {J : Type w} [Category.{w', w} J] (K : J ⥤ C) (F : C ⥤ D) [HasLimit (K ⋙ F)]
  [CreatesLimit K F] : HasLimit K
```
***
If `F` creates the limit of `K` and `K ⋙ F` has a limit, then `K` has a limit.
